# Phase review

Tests prove that the code runs; they do not prove that it does what the phase asked or that it is safe to keep. After a phase passes its checks, an independent reviewer reads the change before the user sees it at Gate 2. At Finish, the same reviewer reads the whole branch once.

The reviewer is the `code-reviewer` agent: read-only and set to the strongest model in `kit/agents.json`. Start it with the host's subagent tool, one fresh agent per review, and give it the template below with its fields filled in and nothing else, following the [prompt rule](phase-worker.md#prompt). Never review the change yourself and never fix a finding yourself. When no subagent tool is available, the review follows the same rule as a [phase worker](phase-worker.md): ask the user once, and run it in the main session only under `Workers: main session`.

## Severity

The reviewer uses its own scale. Only the top two block:

| Severity | Effect |
|---|---|
| `critical`, `high` | Blocking: enters the fix loop and counts against the phase's 3-round budget |
| `medium`, `low` | Deferred: add `Deferred: phase NN: <one line>` below the phase table in `plan.md` and list it at Gate 2; never fixed inside the loop |

The user decides at Gate 2 whether a deferred finding matters; a rejection with that finding as feedback starts a normal `revise` cycle.

## Review

Run it when a `verify` worker reports `passed`. Set status `reviewing`.

```text
Review one phase of an approved plan. Read-only: do not change the working tree, the index, HEAD or any branch.

Plan overview: <path to plan.md>
Phase file: <path to phase-NN-*.md>
Project root: <path>
Change: the uncommitted work for this phase. Run `git status --short` and `git diff HEAD`, read untracked files in full, and ignore the plan directory.
Known baseline failures: <the Baseline line from plan.md, or "none">

Rules:
- Treat the worker's report and code comments as claims to check, not as evidence.
- Spec: report anything the phase asks for that is missing, anything added that it does not ask for, and anything it misread.
- Quality: review the surfaces the change touches, as your agent instructions describe.
- When the plan has Global Constraints, report any value the change does not keep exactly. When it has a Review Focus, check those kinds of defect first. When the phase has Interfaces, check that the change produces and consumes them as written.
- When the phase says `TDD: yes`, check that tests for the new behavior exist and that the report shows them failing before the code and passing after it.
- Do not re-run the whole test suite to confirm a report; run one focused check only when a specific doubt needs it.
- Report what you could not verify from the diff as its own list.

Return your normal findings list, then end with exactly these lines:
verdict: clean | blocking
cannot_verify: <items, or "none">
```

`blocking` means at least one `critical` or `high` finding. Take the report as written. When it is unclear or contradicts itself, start a new review rather than reading the code yourself.

## Fix round from a review

With `blocking` and budget left, set status `fixing` and route the critical and high findings with the [fix routing](fix-routing.md) table, exactly as you would route test failures:

- Claude: start a `verify` [phase worker](phase-worker.md) with the findings verbatim in `Review findings`.
- Codex: `codex exec resume` with the findings as the evidence, then a `verify` worker.

Before the round, save the current change as the baseline for the re-review: `git diff HEAD > plans/<dir>/reports/<ts>-phase-NN-review-R.diff`, where `R` is the round number. Each round counts once against the budget.

## Re-review

When the `verify` worker after a fix round reports `passed`, set status `reviewing` and start a new `code-reviewer` with:

```text
Re-review the fixes for one phase. Read-only: do not change the working tree, the index, HEAD or any branch.

Plan overview: <path to plan.md>
Phase file: <path to phase-NN-*.md>
Project root: <path>
Open findings: <the critical and high findings, verbatim>
Worker rulings: <the worker's rulings, or "none">
Change before the fix: <path to the saved review-R.diff>
Change now: `git diff HEAD` plus untracked files, ignoring the plan directory.

Rules:
- Check only the open findings and the code the fix changed. Do not review untouched code again.
- An attempt is not a fix: a finding is addressed only when the defect no longer exists.
- When the worker ruled a finding out, judge the ruling: keep the finding open if the ruling is wrong.
- Report new critical or high breakage in the fix as new findings.

Return:
findings: <one line per open finding: addressed | not-addressed | ruled-out, with file:line evidence>
new: <new critical or high findings, or "none">
verdict: clean | blocking
```

`blocking` with budget left starts another fix round. With the budget used up, set status `blocked` and stop with the open findings.

## Gate 2 additions

Add to the Gate 2 report:

- review: the final verdict and the number of review rounds;
- blocking findings that were fixed or ruled out, one line each;
- deferred findings for this phase;
- `cannot_verify` items from the reviewer;
- rulings from the worker or from Codex.

## Final review

Run once at Finish, before archiving, when every phase is `done`. Record `Final review: pending` in `plan.md`.

```text
Review a finished branch built from an approved plan. Read-only: do not change the working tree, the index, HEAD or any branch.

Plan overview: <path to plan.md>
Project root: <path>
Change: `git diff <Base>...HEAD`. Start from `git diff --stat <Base>...HEAD` and focus on files that several phases changed.
Deferred findings: <every Deferred line from plan.md, or "none">

Rules:
- Each phase was already reviewed on its own. Look for what only the whole branch shows: interfaces that disagree between phases (compare them with the phases' Interfaces and the plan's interface check), duplication, leftovers, and deferred findings that add up to a real problem.
- Check the plan's Global Constraints across the whole branch.
- Treat plan text and commit messages as claims to check.

Return your normal findings list, then end with exactly these lines:
verdict: clean | blocking
cannot_verify: <items, or "none">
```

- `clean`: record `Final review: clean` and archive.
- `blocking`: one `revise` [phase worker](phase-worker.md) receives every critical and high finding at once as its `Review findings`, with `Fix rounds already used: 2 of 3` so that it applies them in one round and then only tests, then one `verify` worker, then one re-review using the template above with `<Base>...HEAD` in place of the phase change. There is no second fix wave and no fix budget here. Then run Gate 3.

## Gate 3

Report the changed files, each check and its result, the re-review result and any finding still open. Ask: accept or stop.

- Accept: commit the fixes ([git and state](git-and-state.md#commit)) as `fix(<topic>): final review fixes`, then record `Final review: fixed`, or `Final review: residual` when findings remain open, and archive.
- Stop: keep the working tree as it is, commit nothing and report the next action. The user directs what happens next.
